title: [Performance] Avoid full-buffer copies in compiled embedding token exchange
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? Embedding token exchange mutates slices of persistent, capacity-sized buffers. AOT functionalization can rebuild/copy the entire backing buffers even for a small decode batch, adding unnecessary memory traffic and graph memory. Use invocation-local padding and masking with the existing group AllGather/ReduceScatter APIs. Captured allocations are managed by the ACL graph pool. Keep common exchange lengths, output cropping and PCP-before-TP reduction; no runner changes or new Embedding custom op. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? Lower compiled embedding overhead without configuration or API changes. ### How was this patch tested? #### End-to-end performance **DSV4 Flash W4A8, three-round end-to-end comparison:** A3, 8 NPUs, MRV2, DP1 × TP1 × PCP8 + EP8, FULL_DECODE_ONLY. Parent main `576b1b0c3` vs PR `8ff49a6cd`, with identical hardware/configuration and vLLM `a98247ab4` + error-message-only Python 3.11 compatibility commit `20804fc0f`. Each version used two warm-up batches, then three rounds of 8 concurrent streaming requests with 32 input / 1,024 output tokens (`temperature=0`, `seed=1024`, `ignore_eos=true`). Three-round means: | Metric | main | PR | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | End-to-end output throughput | 197.40 token/s | 212.01 token/s | +7.40% | | Request latency | 41.44 s | 38.58 s | -6.90% | | TTFT | 443.47 ms | 416.06 ms | -6.18% | | Client TPOT | 40.08 ms | 37.31 ms | -6.91% | End-to-end throughput includes prefill, queueing and stream completion. All 48 measured requests passed token-length checks, with zero prefix-cache hits/preemptions and no external NPU processes on the selected devices. Actual FULL graph replay and the compiled embedding exchange path were verified. Historical DSV4.1 W4A8 measurements against main (A3, PCP8, batch 4, 65,536 input / 1,024 output tokens, FULL decode): | Metric | main | Optimized | Reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Server decode TPOT | 47.492 ms | 40.294 ms | 15.16% | | ITL while all four requests decode | 43.104 ms | 35.921 ms | 16.66% | The DSV4.1 figures are single-round historical results. #### Profiling evidence DSV4 Flash W4A8, PCP8 + EP8, concurrency 8, 32 input / 1,024 output tokens; parent main `576b1b0c3` vs PR `b7645500d` (same production code as `8ff49a6cd`, with a CPU-test mock fix). Native torch_npu Level1 captured 16 FULL decode steps on each of 8 ranks, while all 8 requests were decoding; prefill was outside the capture. | Embedding capacity-buffer copies, per rank per decode step | main | PR | |---|---:|---:| | Large TensorMove kernels | 5 | 0 | | Logical bytes copied | 1.625 GiB | 0 | | Summed kernel duration, mean across 8 ranks | 2.677 ms | 0 | The removed copies are three 512 MiB and two 64 MiB tensors per step. Embedding collective payloads are unchanged: AllGather 4 B input / 32 B output; ReduceScatter 64 KiB input / 8 KiB output. The gain comes from removing local full-buffer copies. Kernel-duration sums are not end-to-end latency savings; the +7.40% throughput result above was measured separately without profiling. The first sampled collective includes profiler-start/rank-arrival skew and is not used as steady-state communication latency. **Before:** long `aclnnInplaceCopy_TensorMoveAiCore_TensorMove` kernels in the embedding exchange region. **After:** the capacity-sized copies disappear; token exchange, lookup and masking remain. The screenshots use different zoom levels and selected windows; their selection durations should not be used to calculate a speedup. #### Correctness - 20 focused CPU tests passed, covering AOT functionalization/dynamic shapes, empty input, invalid exchange lengths and output stability across calls. - Full DSV4.1 W8A8 services on A3, DP2 × TP1 × PCP8 with EP: text and real-image inputs under eager, PIECEWISE and FULL_DECODE_ONLY; concurrency 1/3/4/8 and inputs up to 65,536 tokens. All 120 formal requests completed; 1,320 sampled function outputs matched CPU checkpoint lookup elementwise, with zero mismatches. All 2,960 profiled AllGather/ReduceScatter pairs matched the actual N and dtype. - Text graph capture/replay passed with changing inputs. Multimodal embedding runs outside the decoder graph; unequal rank lengths and cropping passed. PIECEWISE capture covered buckets through 128; larger prefill ran uncaptured. - The function-level hardware validation above used `6733d1528`. The subsequent in-place mask change also passed CPU correctness and AOT graph-equivalence checks. These function checks do not measure physical HCCL link bytes. - End-to-end GPQA Diamond on PR `8ff49a6cd`, DSV4 W4A8, the same fixed 100 questions, concurrency 8: **77% / 71% / 77%, mean 75% (range 71–77%)**. All 300 responses completed with zero HTTP failures/timeouts; prompt hashes and native per-question scoring matched. Outputs hitting the 8,192-token cap counted as incorrect (question 79 in all rounds; question 69 also in round 2). Historical results were 70% / 74% / 75% (mean 73%); this is reference only, since main accuracy was not rerun and the historical environment/version differed. --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage** - [x] **Regression test** - [x] **Error / failure path coverage** - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests** - [x] **Performance impact**: three-round DSV4 end-to-end comparison above. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a98247ab4db686ee03c66d5feb3c761e52a2f8ab
